18:34 Local Time, 17:34 GMT, 23:04 IST | Stumps, Day 1: Eventful day and England have a lead of 23 runs at the end of the opening day of the third Test. Having released 7 players from the original squad, Pakistan were forced to make four changes and fielded three debutants. Batting has certainly been their weak link this series and they were inserted to bat on an overcast day. And a familiar story played out. They lost their top four inside the first hour, three more by lunch and were then bundled out for 133 in the 34th over. The top five batters were dismissed for single-digit scores. Saud Shakeel batted positively and top-scored with 43 and Abbas was their second best batter, scoring 21. Ollie Robinson and Jofra Archer accounted for the top four Pakistan batters, finishing with three wickets apiece, while Josh Tongue was once again impressive with a 4-fer.

While it didn't seem like a deck where a team should be bowled out for 133, it was certainly a seam-conducive deck. Ben Duckett kept playing expansive shots and eventually nicked off for 11, Jordan Cox was trapped lbw by Abbas and Root became Razaullah's maiden Test scalp. The English captain was out lbw for the fourth time in as many innings this series. England were reduced to 39/3. The tension was palpable, marked by a few plays-and-misses and a missed run-out chance. But Brook and Gay managed to survive that and runs started to come at a quicker pace. The left-hand opening batter recorded a patient fifty and was involved in a century partnership with Brook. Gay got to his highest Test score but couldn't kick on as he fell to Razaullah. Abbas beat Brook's edge numerous times before the stylish right-hander raised his 20th Test fifty.

So how did the three debutants fare? Ghazi Ghori got off the mark with a blazing upper cut but was beaten for pace and trapped lbw off his 5th ball. Imran Randhawa bowled 6 overs but couldn't exert any sort of pressure. Razaullah, the slingy pacer, certainly enjoyed his first day in international cricket. He bowled consistently at 140+ kph and dismissed the England captain in his first over. Although he doled out a few freebies and conceded a few boundaries, he came back late in the day to bowl another testing spell. Razaullah broke the 104-run stand and showed a lot of promise.
